label: Claude Fable 5.2
output:
To: docs/climate-programme/border-revenues-launch/handover
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Handover for Inês: launch Thursday 26 November

Inês,

My father is ill and I am with my family. I don't know yet for how long, so you will have to do Thursday without me. I am sorry, and most of all for the state I am leaving it in. Everything you need is below, in the order I would do it.

THE PROBLEM

This afternoon I found an error in figure 3. The figure and the summary used the 2030 revenue estimate from the old run, without the free allocation phase-out. The correct number for 2030 LDC-relevant revenue is EUR 1.4 billion, not EUR 2.1 billion. The conclusion of the paper does not change, but the headline number does.

- Corrected: PDF v7 on the drive (pages 3, 14 and 15).
- Not corrected: deck v4 (slides 6 and 9).
- Not corrected: the embargoed press release, which went to 34 Brussels contacts on Friday and says 2.1.

My note with the details is in this folder ("ERROR figure 3").

TUESDAY

1. Hanna and the press release. This comes first. The embargo lifts Thursday at 10:00, and every hour the wrong number sits with 34 journalists is a risk. Assume Hanna does not have the details yet. She needs to send a corrected release with 1.4, and a short line saying the figure was corrected. If she wants a senior name on it, Geert can sign off. He knows I am away.

2. Tomás at Lindqvist's office. Please write to him yourself (tomas.reyes@ep-office-lindqvist.example) and tell him you are presenting and sitting on the panel instead of me. He wrote this morning with a change: the MEP has a vote and must leave at 13:30. So the presentation is 15 minutes instead of 20 and the panel starts at 12:50. She wants to take at least two questions herself before she goes. Please confirm that to him. Ask him also who chairs after 13:30 and whether we still close at 14:00, because the run of show in this folder is the old one.

3. The deck. Change 2.1 to 1.4 on slides 6 and 9, and check the chart on slide 9 itself, not only the text. Then cut it to 15 minutes. You made it 14 slides already, and you know better than me what else can go. My speaker notes are still in there. Throw out whatever doesn't sound like you.

WEDNESDAY

4. Badges, before 12:00. Tomás needs the final names of everyone from our side by Wednesday 12:00, otherwise security will not let them in. Take me off and make sure you are on, plus whoever you want with you.

5. Press calls at 14:00 and 15:00. Two journalists asked for a background call, one from a trade newsletter and one from a Belgian daily. Hanna told them I would be available. They are by phone, 20 minutes each, and they are in my calendar. I would like you to take them, since you know the paper as well as I do. If it is too much the day before, ask Hanna to move them or do them herself with your notes. Either way, make sure both have the corrected release before they call.

THURSDAY

Everyone must be at the security entrance of the Altiero Spinelli building by 12:00. Tomás collects the badges. There is a light lunch outside the room from 12:00.

12:30 welcome by Lindqvist (5 min)
12:35 your presentation (15 min)
12:50 panel: Abena Owusu-Mensah (remote), Florian Kessler, you. Lindqvist moderates.
13:30 Lindqvist leaves
After that Q&A and close, depending on what Tomás says.

Abena's remote link is in the calendar invite. You know that already, you wrote it to me.

Make sure v7 is the only version of the PDF that goes anywhere.

About the 2.1: the mistake is mine, not yours. If anyone asks, say so, in those words. I would mention the correction yourself in one sentence when you come to the revenue chart, so nobody else gets to bring it up first. It is an old model run. We found it and fixed it, and the conclusion stands. Don't go further than that.

Kessler will try to make the whole panel about the 80% pass-through. His written comments are in the folder and so are my reply lines, but honestly you don't need them, because you ran the annex B sensitivity runs yourself. 80% is the central case. We ran 40% and 60%. The result holds at 60% and weakens at 40%. Say that openly and without getting defensive, and then go back to what the paper is about. He should not set the tone. On resource shuffling we agree it is a risk. It is in section 5.2, and we recommend the Commission's monitoring report. Abena will probably back us on the LDC side. She was strong on the call.

AFTER

Lucy Tran from the Halvorsen Foundation is coming with a colleague. For their grant report she needs two photos from the event and the attendance numbers by 4 December. Ask someone to take pictures and count the room, so you don't have to think about it.

REACHING ME

You can call me. Tonight or early tomorrow is best. After 9 tomorrow morning I might not pick up. Send me a message then and I will call back when I can. If you can't reach me, decide yourself. I mean that. Whatever you decide, I will stand behind it.

AND THE REST

I trust you completely with this. That is not something I say to make you feel better. In Lisbon the projector died in the middle of my panel and you rescued it while I was still looking at the cable. You are better live than you think you are. The paper is as much yours as mine, and Lucy said the same when she congratulated us both.

I am sorry to hand you a mistake of mine to clean up two days before the launch. You deserved a better handover than this.

Marieke
